purpose: Define a contemporary retained/disrupted channel classification for Izu that is independent of focal floral phenotype and reproductive outcome, so Issue #91 can connect channel state to visitation, SVD and effective service without treating historical non-report as proven loss.
source_reference: mainland Shizuoka/Chiba large-bumblebee channel; source availability already frozen in data/design/izu_h5_source_retention_prefreeze_20260909.json

state_rule.retained: source_state=available AND at least one independent channel detection under usable survey effort
state_rule.disrupted: source_state=available AND zero independent channel detections under usable survey effort AND prespecified probability of at least one detection if the channel were present is >=0.95
state_rule.unresolved: all other source-available cases, including zero detections with insufficient detection probability

allowed_calibration: independent repeat surveys within the same survey method
source/reference channel detections collected under the same method
a prespecified occupancy/detection model fitted without floral phenotype or reproductive outcomes
prohibited_calibration: choose threshold to reproduce historical Oshima-to-southern-island pattern
use floral size, floral syndrome, mating system, autonomous assurance, fruit set or seed set
set detection probability from climatic compatibility alone

survey_independence.preferred: channel survey not conditioned on focal plant response; standardized transect, timed search, trap, or community-wide visitor survey with explicit effort
survey_independence.rule: The independent channel-state survey and focal-plant visitation may occur in the same site/event but must remain separately recorded estimands.

historical_evidence_role.reason: Inoue source-locked tables support main-pollinator replacement/non-report under effort but the existing audit explicitly forbids converting omitted Bombus rows into proven absence.

next_links: focal-plant visit bouts per monitored flower-hour

claim_boundary: A contemporary disrupted state identifies an effort-aware current channel deficit relative to a source-available channel. It does not by itself identify historical extinction, historical selection, or the timing of floral evolution.
